results.title: Every Brown Tip Explained (Why Your Plant Has Brown Crispy Edges)
results.description:
Your plant has brown tips. And the reason is almost certainly not what you think it is.
Brown tips are the most misdiagnosed houseplant symptom — and the most common fix people try makes them worse. If your plant has brown crispy tips, brown edges, or brown patches and you don't know why, this video covers all seven causes, every pattern, and exactly what to do about each one.
The most important thing before you watch: brown leaf tips on houseplants are almost never a watering problem.

───────────────────────────────────────────
QUICK BROWN TIP REFERENCE — save this
───────────────────────────────────────────
Crispy brown tips spreading inward from the very tip, oldest leaves first, rest of leaf healthy green → Low humidity
Similar to above but with a yellow-brown boundary, on Peace Lily, Calathea, Spider Plant or Dracaena → Fluoride in tap water
Tips browning faster on one side of plant, plant near any vent or fan → Dry airflow from heating or air conditioning

Brown tips appearing or worsening after fertilising, white crust on soil surface → Fertiliser burn — flush the soil immediately
Brown tips combined with watering much more often than before, roots at drainage holes → Root bound — repot one size up
Isolated brown patch at one specific point, other leaves unaffected → Cold glass or physical contact damage

results.title: Why Your Plant Has Brown Tips (It's Not Lack of Water)
results.description:
Brown leaf tips. You've seen them. Maybe you're staring at one right now.

Every gardener does the same thing. They grab the watering can. But what if that's the one move making it worse?

In this video, I break down the real causes behind brown leaf tips—and almost none of them have anything to do with how much you're watering. You'll learn how salt buildup from fertiliser quietly suffocates roots, why fluoride in tap water accumulates at the tips of sensitive plants, and how the air around your plant might be drying it out faster than the roots can keep up. Plus, two bonus causes and three common myths that don't actually fix anything.

By the end, you'll have a simple four‑question checklist to diagnose exactly what's wrong with your plant—and how to fix it.

Timestamps:
0:00 – Brown tips? Don't grab the watering can

Stop watering your plants just because of brown leaf tips. You are likely missing the real cause behind the damage.

Most gardeners reach for the watering can the moment they see crispy edges, but that often makes the situation worse. If you are checking the soil and finding it damp while the foliage continues to brown, the issue lies elsewhere. Understanding proper houseplant care means looking past the surface to identify what is actually stressing your greenery.

Salt buildup from fertilizer can quietly suffocate roots, while fluoride in tap water often accumulates at the tips of sensitive varieties. Dry air can also pull moisture faster than roots can keep up, leading to common plant problems that water alone cannot fix. Use this simple four-question checklist to perform a quick plant diagnosis and get your collection back to health.
